recall.question: What does this lesson cover?
recall.answer: Sequence models that factor the joint law left to right: the chain rule, conditional densities, discrete tokens, teacher forcing, causal networks, the transformer, sampling, exact likelihood, context cost, masked objectives, and flow matching.

recall.question: What will the learner be able to do after this lesson?
recall.answer: Factor a joint law by hand, write a conditional table, compute NLL and perplexity on a toy, explain teacher forcing and exposure bias, read a causal mask, work one attention head by hand, and sample at three temperatures.

recall.question: State the sequence toy numbers.
State the attention toy numbers.

keyTerms.definition: Factors any joint law into a product of conditionals, one per position.
Left to right: the order is a choice; the product is order-free.

recall.question: Evaluate p(abc) on the toy.
Does the reverse order give the same joint?
recall.answer: Yes: p(c) x p(b|c) x p(a|b,c) is also 0.05 with different factors.

keyTerms.definition: One row per context; each row sums to 1.
Each row is a vector in the V-simplex.

recall.question: What is the next-token law after 'a'?
recall.answer: (0.35, 0.4, 0.25); the most likely next token is b at 0.4.

recall.question: Why not tabulate all contexts?
recall.answer: V^L possible contexts: the network generalizes across them instead.

keyTerms.definition: V = 50,000 makes the softmax the cost center.
Negative log-likelihood: 0.4076 for token c on the toy.

recall.question: Compute the softmax and NLL for logits (1,2,3), token c.
What does tokenization decide?
recall.answer: What the atoms are; changing it changes every probability.

keyTerms.definition: Feeds ground-truth prefixes during training: fast, parallel, stable.
The model never learns to recover from its own mistakes.

recall.question: What is the train/sample mismatch on 'abc'?
recall.answer: Training uses true 'a' to predict b; sampling may draw 'c' first and condition off-distribution.

recall.question: What closes the gap, and at what cost?
recall.answer: Scheduled sampling mixes in model predictions, at the cost of serial non-differentiable training.

keyTerms.definition: Lower triangular: position 2 reads positions 1 and 2, never 3.
No gradient path from the future to the past exists.

recall.question: How many ones and zeros in the 3x3 mask?
recall.answer: 6 ones, 3 zeros. Position 3 sees all three; position 1 sees only itself.

recall.question: What happens with one unmasked layer?
recall.answer: The future leaks through the whole network.

keyTerms.definition: A data-dependent weighted average: scores, softmax, mix values.
Multiple heads run attention in parallel subspaces.

recall.question: Work the toy attention head.
Why scale by 1/sqrt(d_k)?
recall.answer: It keeps dot products O(1) at init so the softmax starts diffuse.

keyTerms.definition: The exploration knob: low T exploits, high T explores.
Nucleus sampling: truncate the tail, then sample.

recall.question: What are the toy distributions at T = 0.5, 1, 2?
What are the T limits?
recall.answer: T -> 0 is argmax; T -> infinity is uniform.

keyTerms.definition: exp(mean NLL): the effective branching factor per token; 2.7144 on the toy.
Two AR models' NLLs are directly comparable on the same tokenization.

recall.question: Compute log p(abc) and perplexity.
recall.answer: log p = -2.9957 nats; perplexity = exp(2.9957/3) = 2.7144.

recall.question: When is an NLL comparison meaningless?
recall.answer: Across tokenizations.

keyTerms.definition: Trades memory for recompute: 256 KB per layer per sequence at L=512, d=64, fp32.
Doubling the context quadruples the attention cost.

recall.question: What is the attention cost at L = 512, d = 64?
recall.answer: L^2 x d = 16.8M mults per head per layer for the scores alone.

recall.question: Why does generating L tokens cost O(L^2) with caching?
recall.answer: Each new token attends to all past tokens.

keyTerms.definition: A representation objective: p(b|a,c) with both sides visible; not a generative law.
Need not come from one joint law.

recall.question: Why can't you ancestrally sample a BERT-style model?
recall.answer: Its conditionals are incompatible: no joint law, no sampler; generation must iterate Gibbs-style.

keyTerms.definition: Learns an ODE directly: regress v_theta(x_t,t) onto the known endpoint velocity.
x_t = (1-t) x_0 + t x_1: the simplest noise-to-data path.

recall.question: Compute the toy flow-matching loss.
recall.answer: Target velocity 2, predicted 1.8: loss (2-1.8)^2 = 0.04.

recall.question: How does sampling work?
recall.answer: Integrate the learned ODE; no noise schedule.

keyTerms.definition: Report each family's own metric: NLL for exact, bound with gap for VAE, samples for GAN.
An AR model with 10x the parameters beating a tiny flow proves nothing about the family.

recall.question: What are the four families' toy numbers?
recall.answer: AR -2.9957 exact; flow about -2.9957 plus dequantization gap; VAE bound -3.4; GAN no number.

recall.question: What does the VAE bound -3.4 hide?
recall.answer: A true -2.9 (better than the flow) or -3.4: the bound does not say.
